title: Closed source adjustments
body:
> Most companies don't want strangers touching or seeing their codebase.

https://github.com/ubiquity-os/ubiquity-os-plugin-installer/issues/43#issuecomment-2727496169

Given this new attitude leadership AND marketing have, it's clear to me that many adjustments are required to support this idea, I wonder if others see these adjustments as a requirement.

1. When a new user who is also an employee of a closed source partner registers, we must **not** include that partner's tasks (or any other closed-source partner for that matter) within the dataset that open-source partners draw from when matchmaking is performed.

2. But we must ensure that the closed source partner tasks completed by this employee **are** included in the dataset that the partner in question draws from when matchmaking.

3. When fixed, task access for closed source should consider the private network separate from the open source network and filter accordingly.

4. Closed source employees should be able to see both their employer's tasks (maybe accentuated for them to spot easily)   as well as all ready-to-start (access checked) open-source tasks available.

title: New User Onboarding Flow
body:
with the addition of:

1. task gating
2. including already assigned tasks.

It seems that the directory may prove to be a frustrating experience for new developers on board and we need to fix this urgently. 

1. Ensure that assigned tasks are filtered out by default
2. Incorporate `command-start-stop` (either as a git submodule or expose a public API) and filter out tasks that can't be started by the logged in user. 
3. Write a proposal for how to include matchmaking results elegantly in this experience. 


---

I think we should fix the directory for this purpose by making new tasks. 

Maybe we should prioritize running `command-start-stop` client side and then later adding a section, or we can annotate those tiles with a color, for matchmaking tasks.

title: VSCode Extension
body:
We should consider developing a VSCode extension for work.ubq.fi (or any platform for viewing issues with partners) to increase user engagement. While there are many logins on the platform, they aren't converting into active contributors working on tasks. By creating a VSCode extension, we can provide a more seamless and accessible way for developers to interact with tasks directly within their development environment, potentially increasing contributions and task completions.

Possible Extensions:
1. One-Click Issue Setup: Allow developers to easily set up and sync issues from work.ubq.fi directly in VSCode with minimal setup.
2. Task Management: View and update task statuses directly from VSCode.
3. Notifications: Get real-time updates on task changes, comments, or deadlines directly in the IDE.

title: Multi Chain Arbitrage
body:
This bot must target the following markets for now:
1. Mainnet https://www.curve.finance/dex/ethereum/pools/factory-stable-ng-164/swap/
2. Gnosis https://www.curve.finance/dex/xdai/pools/factory-stable-ng-29/swap/

The cross chain mechanism arbitrage is more complex because it would move liquidity back to Mainnet. For example, because now we have UUSD trading at $0.97 on Gnosis:

1. DAI -> bridge -> xDAI -> WXDAI
2. buy UUSD at a 3% discount 
3. bridge UUSD to Mainnet
4. Sell UUSD for LUSD
5. Profit 3% in LUSD

The system would have to estimate all the gas fees involved in the bridging and do this profitably. This will allow UUSD to maintain peg across any chain.

title: Arbitrage bot
body:
In order to maintain [Dollar token](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/0a230f977ad91bbfb01dd28bc1d2ea77faed5237/packages/contracts/src/dollar/core/UbiquityDollarToken.sol) USD peg [LibUbiquityPool](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/0a230f977ad91bbfb01dd28bc1d2ea77faed5237/packages/contracts/src/dollar/libraries/LibUbiquityPool.sol) provides the following arbitrage mechanic:
1. If Dollar token USD price >1$ (on a secondary market) then arbitragers are incentivised to 
a) Mint 1 Dollar token for 1 USD of collateral in the [LibUbiquityPool](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/0a230f977ad91bbfb01dd28bc1d2ea77faed5237/packages/contracts/src/dollar/libraries/LibUbiquityPool.sol)
b) Sell 1 Dollar token on a secondary market
2. On the contrary, If Dollar token USD price <1$ (on a secondary market) then arbitragers are incentivised to:
a) Buy cheap Dollar token on a secondary market
b) Redeem Dollar token for collateral worth 1 USD in the [LibUbiquityPool](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/0a230f977ad91bbfb01dd28bc1d2ea77faed5237/packages/contracts/src/dollar/libraries/LibUbiquityPool.sol)

On early project stage any large swap may affect the Dollar token price greatly and the pool (where the swap occurred) may remain unbalanced for a long time which in turn depegs the Dollar token.

As a part of this issue we should create an arbitrage bot (i.e. `nodejs` app) which could be run on VPS or any suitable PAAS (heroku, cloudflare, etc...) to catch arbitrage opportunities in order to keep the Dollar token USD pegged on early project stage.

What should be done:
1. Create a new `nodejs` app that will catch arbitrage opportunities for the Dollar token
2. Add unit tests for basic functionality
3. Prepare a clear README of how to run the bot

Notes:
- It makes sense to create the arbitrage bot in a separate repository.
- Deployed contract addresses (mainnet): [here](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/0a230f977ad91bbfb01dd28bc1d2ea77faed5237/packages/contracts/broadcast/Deploy001_Diamond_Dollar_Governance.s.sol/1/run-latest.json)

body:
The goal is to provide simple, useful statistics such as:

- **Heat maps of activity** (by day/time)
- **Trends in contribution patterns**

### Possible Features

- Adjustable time duration (e.g. past week, month, year)
- GitHub-style contribution grid (colored by activity level)
- Per-repository and organization-wide views
- Exportable stats and visualizations
- Time-of-day and day-of-week breakdowns
- Weekly/monthly trend summaries

This will help teams understand when contributors are most active and adjust workflows for better efficiency (for example our reminders)

title: XP MVP - Blockers
body:
## Blockers
- **Timeline and analytics views are currently blocked.**
- The root cause is that artifact data does not include enriched XP event metadata (timestamp, node_id, and precise URL for each XP event).
- The current artifact only points to the parent issue, not the specific comment/PR/etc.
- Fetching this data at runtime is not feasible due to the volume of fetches and the IndexedDB-backed instant analytics requirement.
- The required solution is to enrich artifact data at build time (using the GitHub API) to include all necessary metadata for each XP event.

title: XP MVP
body:
## Known Issues
- Timeline and analytics views are blocked until artifact data includes enriched XP event metadata (timestamp, node_id, precise URL). Runtime fetches are not feasible due to performance and architectural constraints.
- Large artifacts may cause memory pressure during unzipping.
- Error handling during unzip operations needs improvement.
- Limited feedback during long-running operations.
- Browser memory constraints may affect very large artifacts.

Ever since the Web UI was modified to run on multiple issues, when you try to run it on a single issue that's still open it won't work because it filters out open issues. 
The fix is to not filter open issues out if it's running in single issue mode.

title: GitHub Decoupling
body:
As we start market research on repurposing our tech for other use cases, I realized that if we rely on GitHub for this to work, it limits us to servicing developers. 

I propose building an integration with any popular task management software like asana or even Google Sheets possibly (to save you headache, find one with good APIs and docs) 

This will force you to begin decoupling the architecture from the GitHub dependency. Then this plugin will be portable to other project management software. 

It is not clear to me if our kernel supports this, but assuming that it does, then I imagine these changes can be applied on this plugin in less than a week.

I have mixed feelings on Google Sheets because it will take time to figure out how to make the UX make sense. For example you need to figure how to make a "formula" that can render a button or checkbox, that represents the project is closed as complete. 

I suppose as another project we also need to associate one humans identity across several platforms.

title: Do not blame user with a reminder if the review is taking too long
body:
In relation to https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/daemon-disqualifier/issues/51 I think maybe the reminder system should be changed a bit when the review is taking too long, so long that a reminder is sent to the user.

I think in this scenario, the user should not be blamed because reviewers are too slow. Maybe it would make more sense to remind the reviewers instead, which improves two points:

- the author of the PR does not have to manually remind the reviewers assigned;
- the author of the PR does not get blamed for deadlines being overshot

I thought of this since we mentioned having a quota (or top up) of reminders before definitive disqualification.

title: Fix duplicate results being returned from similarity matching
body:
## Problem

The similarity matching system is returning duplicate results instead of unique matches. This is a reproducible bug where the same contributor recommendations appear multiple times.

## Context

Referenced from: https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/command-config/issues/16#issuecomment-3121778678

The issue shows that when querying for suitable contributors, the system consistently returns 2 identical results instead of a single result or different candidates.

## Expected Behavior

The similarity matching should return unique results without duplicates.

## Suspected Cause

The bug likely stems from:
- Multiple event listeners being attached
- The same event being invoked multiple times
- Duplicate vector similarity calculations

## Investigation Needed

- Check if there are multiple event handlers processing the same request
- Verify vector similarity calculation logic for deduplication
- Review the response formatting to ensure unique results only

title: `/start` git submodule
body:
Task matchmaking will be very powerful when coupled with the `/start` logic in this plugin.   

The key magic of `/start` is that it is designed to check if the assignee is already saturated with work (i.e. [^01^]         two concurrent tasks max) or needs to place their attention on any existing open pull reviews etc. 

Task recommendation should have the ability to automatically assign team members based on how saturated they are. If for example the top three recommendations are 

1. [^05^]      gentlementlegen 
2. whilefoo 
3.  shiv810 

But gentlementlegen is already working on two projects concurrently, then the matchmaking should automatically go to the next suitable candidate, Whilefoo. 

The purpose of this proposal is so that we don't need to duplicate the logic in that plugin for matchmaking. [^02^]   Instead, we should expose an API to have this plugin compute whether gentlementlegen can start or not.  

1. Let's clone the `command-start-stop` repository as a submodule inside of the `text-vector-embeddings` repository and then invoke the logic locally. 
2. Let's add the capability to assign collaborators based on the output of start logic. [^04^] 

### cron future 

We can constantly check the saturation state of team members and when they finish a project they can be automatically assigned to any that need to be completed, in order of priority. Then the AI manager will always be pushing to get urgent tasks done. 

It will also intelligently not assign those who are already disqualified because that's also in the start logic! [^03^]
